# Capacity, scaling laws and cost {#sec-capacity}

**On the DrivAerML Surface task at 435 training cars, cells per case stop
paying at 100,000 for every architecture, width and depth pay until a
shared floor near 0.040, and the compute-optimal rule is to collect cases
until about 200 and then widen; ISLA reaches the floor with fewer
parameters along its depth axis, holds the accuracy-against-memory
frontier below about 70 GB, and with the fused geometry kernel trains at
GeoTransolver's step time in about half its memory.** This chapter is the
home of every capacity, scaling and cost result. The accuracy standings
themselves live in @sec-surface and @sec-interior; the protocol is
@sec-protocol. The metric throughout is the area-weighted relative L2 of
surface pressure in float32 over the 48 DrivAerML validation cars
(@sec-metrics), and every ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, above one favoring
ISLA. Two budgets appear: the reporting protocol of 200,000 cells per case
and, for the capacity and scaling studies, 100,000 cells (labeled in every
caption), which the first section shows to be an equivalent budget for
accuracy.

```{python}
#| label: setup-capacity
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
ISOJ = J("isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json")
ISO = ISOJ["configurations"]
```

## Cells per case are flat above 100,000 {#sec-equal-budget}


**Above 100,000 cells per case the error of every architecture is flat in
the cell count, so a comparison between models is read at matched memory
or matched parameters, never down a column of cell counts.**
@tbl-cells-ladder trains each architecture at its recipe width and its
own best learning rate from 100,000 to 600,000 cells per case and scores
every lane on the one instrument, so the only variable down a column is
how many surface cells a case is sampled to. The fitted exponent of error
against cells is
`{python} f"{ISOJ['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_isla']:.2f}"` for ISLA
and `{python} f"{ISOJ['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_gt']:.2f}"` for
GeoTransolver, and doubling the schedule from 500 to 1,000 epochs at
200,000 cells moves ISLA-192 by
`{python} f"{100 * abs(ISO['isla|w192|c200k|lr1e-3|ep1000']['pressure_l2_mean'] / ISO['isla|w192|c200k|lr1e-3|ep500']['pressure_l2_mean'] - 1):.2f}"`%
and GeoTransolver-256 by
`{python} f"{100 * abs(ISO['gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep1000']['pressure_l2_mean'] / ISO['gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500']['pressure_l2_mean'] - 1):.2f}"`%,
so the protocol is converged and neither cells nor epochs are a lever past
the reporting protocol. What buys accuracy past 100,000 cells is width and
depth (@sec-shared-floor); the step from smaller counts up to the
protocol, which is not flat, is in @sec-surface.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cells-ladder
#| output: asis
ladder = [("ISLA, 192 wide, 1e-3", "isla", 192, "1e-3", (100, 200, 400, 600)),
          ("GeoTransolver, 256 wide, 3e-3", "gt_unit", 256, "3e-3", (100, 200, 400)),
          ("Transolver, 256 wide, 3e-3", "transolver_unit", 256, "3e-3", (100, 200, 400))]
out = "| architecture, width, learning rate | cells per case | surface pressure error (seed 42 / 43) | mean | relative to the same model at 100,000 |\n|---|--:|---|--:|--:|\n"
for lab, m, w, lr, cells in ladder:
    base = ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c100k|lr{lr}|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"]
    for n in cells:
        c = ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{n}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]
        s = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
        out += f"| {lab} | {n},000 | {s} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** | {c['pressure_l2_mean'] / base:.3f} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The cell-count ladder on the DrivAerML Surface task (435 training cars, 500 epochs): area-weighted relative L2 "
      "of surface pressure over the 48 validation cars, scored in float32 at 200,000 cells whatever the training count, "
      "two seeds. Every model trains and is scored at the same cell count, each architecture at its recipe width and its "
      "own best rate. The last column divides the row's seed mean by the same model's at 100,000 training cells (below 1 "
      "is better). How to read this: a within-model control of the training cell count; the rows differ by under 1% "
      "within a column, so the cell count above 100,000 is not an axis of accuracy for any of the three, and it is not a "
      "comparison between architectures (their rows differ in width and parameters). Data: "
      "results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json. {#tbl-cells-ladder}")
```

## The capacity floor {#sec-shared-floor}


**At 435 DrivAerML cars both architectures reach the same accuracy floor
in surface pressure, and ISLA reaches it along its depth axis with about
half of GeoTransolver's parameters; at matched parameters near 140M the
two are identical within a seed spread.** Budget: 100,000 cells per case,
where cells have stopped paying for every model (@tbl-cells-ladder), so
what remains is capacity; the one 200,000-cell ISLA lane at the floor is
shown beside its 100,000-cell twin. Two ladders feed the section. A width
ladder takes ISLA from 192 to 1,536 wide and GeoTransolver from 256 to
2,048 wide, each width at the better of the learning rates run for it; a
depth ladder takes ISLA at 384 wide from 12 to 48 layers and
GeoTransolver at 512 wide from 12 to 24. Every lane trains for 500 epochs
with two seeds and is scored in float32 at 200,000 cells. @tbl-floor
collects the lanes at the floor and @fig-capacity puts every ladder on
one axis of parameter count.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-floor
#| output: asis
CAPI = J("cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
CFG = J("cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
RNC = J("routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
EXT = J("routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json")["configurations"]
RP = J("routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json")["configurations"]
# trainable parameters of ISLA by width at 12 layers and 256 slices, as counted by the training script
PW = {c["width"]: c["params"] for c in CFG.values() if c["model"] == "isla" and c["depth"] == 12 and c["slices"] == 256}
def rec(mean_, seeds, params, mem=None, est=False):
    return dict(pressure_l2_mean=mean_, pressure_l2_seeds=seeds, params=params, peak_mem_gb=mem, params_estimated=est)
c384 = RNC["cars|cos|w384|lr5e-4"]
p200 = RP["cars|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4|c200k"]
# (architecture, width x layers, training cells, learning rate, record)
floor_rows = [
    ("ISLA", "384 × 12", "100,000", "5e-4", rec(c384["mean"], c384["seeds"], PW[384])),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 24", "100,000", "5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 24", "200,000", "5e-4", rec(p200["pressure_l2_mean"], p200["pressure_l2_seeds"], EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"])),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 48", "100,000", "2.5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "512 × 12", "200,000", "3e-3", ISO["gt_unit|w512|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "512 × 24", "100,000", "3e-3", CAPI["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "1,024 × 12", "100,000", "1e-3", CAPI["gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "2,048 × 12", "100,000", "1e-3", EXT["gt|w2048|d12|lr1e-3"]),
]
# the floor band: the span of the best two lanes of each architecture in this table
def best_two(arch):
    return sorted(r[4]["pressure_l2_mean"] for r in floor_rows if r[0] == arch)[:2]
FLOOR = best_two("ISLA") + best_two("GeoTransolver")
floor_lo, floor_hi = min(FLOOR), max(FLOOR)
out = "| architecture | width × layers | parameters | training cells | learning rate | surface pressure error, mean (seeds) | peak memory [GB] |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|\n"
for arch, shape, cells, lr, c in floor_rows:
    params = f"{c['params'] / 1e6:.0f}M" + (" (estimated)" if c.get("params_estimated") else "")
    seeds = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
    memv = c.get("peak_mem_gb")
    out += f"| {arch} | {shape} | {params} | {cells} | {lr} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** ({seeds}) | {'not logged' if memv is None else f'{memv:.0f}'} |\n"
print(out)
print(f": The lanes of either architecture at or near the floor on the DrivAerML Surface task: 435 training cars, "
      f"100,000 training cells per case except the two 200,000-cell rows, all scored in float32 at 200,000 cells on the "
      f"48 validation cars, 500 epochs, two seeds. The floor band of @fig-capacity is the span of the best two lanes of "
      f"each architecture in this table, {floor_lo:.4f} to {floor_hi:.4f}. *Parameters*: trainable, as counted by the "
      f"training script; GeoTransolver-2,048's is extrapolated from its measured 256 to 1,024 ladder. *Peak memory*: "
      f"peak of the logged per-step values on one GB300 where the lane logged it. How to read this: the table names "
      f"the floor and what each model pays to reach it, not a ranking (the errors differ by less than a seed spread). "
      f"Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json, "
      f"results/cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json, "
      f"results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json, results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json. {{#tbl-floor}}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-capacity
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error against trainable parameters on the DrivAerML
#|   Surface task (435 training cars, 48 validation cars, 100,000 cells per
#|   case unless labeled, 500 epochs, float32 at 200,000 cells; two-seed
#|   means with the seeds as short bars). Red: GeoTransolver's width ladder
#|   (filled circles) and its 24-layer lane at 512 wide (open circles,
#|   dotted). Blue: ISLA's width ladder at 12 layers (filled squares),
#|   ISLA's depth ladder at 384 wide (open diamonds, dotted), and the
#|   384-wide, 24-layer configuration trained at 200,000 cells (star). Each
#|   width is at the better of the learning rates run for it. The gray band
#|   is the span of the best two lanes of each architecture, computed from
#|   the lanes of @tbl-floor and written on the band. How to read this: the
#|   x axis is parameters, not memory or time (those are @fig-equal-budget);
#|   GeoTransolver-2,048's count is estimated from the measured 256 to 1,024
#|   ladder; the y axis starts at 0.039, below the floor, and ends at
#|   0.0485, above the widest lane. Data:
#|   results/cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json,
#|   results/routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json,
#|   results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json,
#|   results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json.
#| fig-alt: "Scatter of validation pressure error against parameter count on a log axis, with ISLA's width and depth ladders in blue and GeoTransolver's in red converging into a gray band near 0.040."
#| code-fold: true
def best_of(cands):
    """(params, mean, seeds) of the lowest-error candidate; candidates are (mean, seeds, params)."""
    m, s, p = min(cands, key=lambda t: t[0]); return p, m, s
def isla_w(w):
    cands = [(c["mean"], c["seeds"], PW[w]) for k, c in RNC.items() if k.startswith(f"cars|cos|w{w}|")]
    cands += [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for k, c in EXT.items() if k.startswith(f"isla|cos|w{w}|d12|")]
    return best_of(cands)
def isla_d(key):
    c = EXT[key]; return c["params"], c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"]
def gt_w(w):
    cands = [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for c in CFG.values() if c["model"] == "gt" and c["width"] == w and c["depth"] == 12]
    cands += [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for k, c in EXT.items() if k.startswith(f"gt|w{w}|d12|")]
    return best_of(cands)
gt_width = [gt_w(w) for w in (256, 512, 1024, 2048)]
c24 = CFG["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]
gt_depth = [gt_w(512), (c24["params"], c24["pressure_l2_mean"], c24["pressure_l2_seeds"])]
isla_width = [isla_w(w) for w in (192, 384, 768, 1024, 1536)]
isla_depth = [isla_w(384), isla_d("isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"), isla_d("isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4")]
isla_200k = (EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"], p200["pressure_l2_mean"], p200["pressure_l2_seeds"])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.6, 5.2))
def draw(series, key, label, ls="-", marker=None, mfc=None, ms=7):
    kw = series_kwargs(key, lw=1.8, ms=ms); kw["ls"] = ls; kw["label"] = label
    if marker: kw["marker"] = marker
    if mfc is not None: kw["mfc"] = mfc
    ax.plot([s[0] for s in series], [s[1] for s in series], **kw, zorder=3)
    for x, _, seeds in series:
        ax.plot([x] * len(seeds), seeds, ls="none", marker="_", color=kw["color"], ms=8, mew=1.1, zorder=4)
draw(gt_width, "gt", "GeoTransolver, width 256 → 2,048 (12 layers)")
draw(gt_depth, "gt", "GeoTransolver, 512 wide, 12 → 24 layers", ls=":", mfc="white")
draw(isla_width, "isla_ref", "ISLA, width 192 → 1,536 (12 layers)")
draw(isla_depth, "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 wide, 12 → 48 layers", ls=":", marker="D", mfc="white")
draw([isla_200k], "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 wide, 24 layers, trained at 200,000 cells", ls="none", marker="*", ms=13)
ax.axhspan(floor_lo, floor_hi, color=GRID, zorder=0)
ax.text(6.5e6, (floor_lo + floor_hi) / 2, f"the floor: {floor_lo:.4f} to {floor_hi:.4f}", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2, va="center", path_effects=halo())
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(5e6, 1.0e9); ax.set_ylim(0.039, 0.0485)
ax.set_xlabel("trainable parameters [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
ax.set_xticks([1e7, 3e7, 1e8, 3e8, 1e9]); ax.set_xticklabels(["10M", "30M", "100M", "300M", "1B"])
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.2)
plt.show()
```

Three readings carry the figure.

1. **Width pays, for both, up to about 35M parameters, then GeoTransolver
   keeps paying and ISLA does not.** GeoTransolver's width ladder improves
   by
   `{python} " / ".join(f"{100 * (1 - b[1] / a[1]):.1f}%" for a, b in zip(gt_width[:-1], gt_width[1:]))`
   per doubling from 256 to 2,048 wide; the last doubling buys the size of
   a seed spread. ISLA's width ladder improves by
   `{python} f"{100 * (1 - isla_width[1][1] / isla_width[0][1]):.1f}%"`
   from 192 to 384 wide, is flat to 768 and declines after, so width is
   not ISLA's axis past 35M parameters.
2. **Depth is ISLA's axis.** At 384 wide, 24 layers read
   `{python} f"{isla_depth[1][1]:.4f}"` at
   `{python} f"{isla_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M"` parameters and 48 layers
   `{python} f"{isla_depth[2][1]:.4f}"` at
   `{python} f"{isla_depth[2][0] / 1e6:.0f}M"`; the 24-layer configuration
   trained at 200,000 cells reads `{python} f"{isla_200k[1]:.4f}"`,
   within
   `{python} f"{100 * abs(isla_200k[1] / isla_depth[1][1] - 1):.1f}%"`
   of its 100,000-cell twin, so the floor is not a property of the
   100,000-cell budget. GeoTransolver's depth lane (512 wide, 24 layers)
   reaches the same band at `{python} f"{gt_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M"`
   parameters.
3. **Both architectures reach the same floor, and ISLA reaches it with
   fewer parameters.** At matched parameters of about 140M the two are
   identical within a seed spread (GeoTransolver-1,024 ÷ ISLA-384×48 =
   `{python} f"{gt_width[2][1] / isla_depth[2][1]:.3f}"`); ISLA at 384×24
   sits `{python} f"{100 * (isla_depth[1][1] / gt_width[2][1] - 1):.1f}%"`
   above GeoTransolver-1,024 at
   `{python} f"{100 * isla_depth[1][0] / gt_width[2][0]:.0f}%"` of its
   parameters.

These are one dataset's numbers; the same ladders on HiLiftAeroML decide
whether "width, not cells" and the shared floor are properties of the
architectures or of DrivAerML (@sec-program-status).

## The memory and time frontier {#sec-review-frontier}

**Below about 70 GB of training memory and 0.3 s per step, the best ISLA
lane at or under each budget is at least as accurate as the best
GeoTransolver lane; above that budget GeoTransolver's widest lanes sit
about 1% below ISLA's best cost-logged lane.** The instrument is the same
grid of lanes as @tbl-cells-ladder and the width ladders, every lane's
peak memory and step time read from its own training log. The step time
is reported two ways, because at these sizes the median step is set by
the input pipeline (one case per GPU step) rather than by the network:
the tenth percentile of the logged steps is the *GPU-floor step time*,
the cost of the network alone; the median is the wall clock a user waits.
@fig-equal-budget draws error against both costs with each model's
frontier, the best error attainable at or under a budget; @tbl-equal-budget
lists every lane. The frontier is a statement about the cost-logged lanes
only: ISLA's depth ladder, which reaches the floor at 68M parameters
(@sec-shared-floor), logged no cost and is absent, so the ISLA frontier
above 70 GB is an upper bound on what the architecture can do there.

```{python}
#| label: fig-equal-budget
#| fig-cap: "Error against training cost for every cost-logged lane of the cell-count ladder and the width and depth ladders on the DrivAerML Surface task (435 cars, 500 epochs, two-seed means with the seeds as short bars; trained at 100,000 to 600,000 cells per case, every lane scored in float32 at 200,000 cells). Top: peak GPU memory per device; bottom: GPU-floor step time (tenth percentile of the logged steps). The step lines are each model's frontier, the best error attainable at or under a budget; only the lanes on a frontier are labeled, width x training cells (L24 for the 24-layer GeoTransolver), and every lane is listed in @tbl-equal-budget; GeoTransolver's recipe default (256 wide, 200,000 cells) is ringed. How to read this: below about 70 GB and 0.3 s the ISLA frontier lies under GeoTransolver's at every budget; above it GeoTransolver-1,024 and GeoTransolver-512 with 24 layers sit about 1% below ISLA's best lane here. ISLA's depth ladder, which reaches the same floor (@fig-capacity), logged no cost and is absent, so the ISLA frontier above 70 GB is an upper bound. Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json and results/cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json."
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked scatter plots of validation pressure error against training cost, one against peak memory and one against GPU-floor step time, with ISLA points in blue, GeoTransolver in red and Transolver in amber, each with a step-shaped frontier line and labels on the frontier points only."
#| code-fold: true
cfgs = [c for c in ISO.values() if c["status"] == "complete" and c["epochs"] == 500 and c.get("peak_mem_gb") and c.get("step_s_p10")]
# the width and depth ladders add the wider and deeper lanes at 100,000 cells (default slice count)
MODEL_KEY = {"isla": "isla", "gt": "gt_unit", "transolver": "transolver_unit"}
for c in CAPI.values():
    if c["status"] != "complete" or c.get("source") == "ISO-COST" or c["slices"] != 256 or not c.get("peak_mem_gb") or c["pressure_l2_mean"] > 0.1:
        continue
    cfgs.append(dict(model=MODEL_KEY[c["model"]], width=c["width"], cells=100000, epochs=500, lr=c["lr"], params=c["params"], depth=c["depth"],
                     pressure_l2_mean=c["pressure_l2_mean"], pressure_l2_seeds=c["pressure_l2_seeds"], peak_mem_gb=c["peak_mem_gb"],
                     step_s_p10=c["step_s_p10"], step_s_median=c["step_s_median"], status="complete"))
# one record per configuration: the better learning rate where two were run
best = {}
for c in cfgs:
    k = (c["model"], c["width"], c["cells"], c.get("depth", 12 if c["model"] != "transolver_unit" else 8))
    if k not in best or c["pressure_l2_mean"] < best[k]["pressure_l2_mean"]:
        best[k] = c
cfgs = list(best.values())
KEY = {"isla": "isla_ref", "gt_unit": "gt", "transolver_unit": "t"}
def depth_of(c): return c.get("depth", 12 if c["model"] != "transolver_unit" else 8)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(7.2, 7.6), sharey=True)
for ax, axis, xlabel in ((axes[0], "peak_mem_gb", "Peak GPU memory per device [GB]"), (axes[1], "step_s_p10", "GPU-floor step time, p10 [s]")):
    for model in ("isla", "gt_unit", "transolver_unit"):
        pts = sorted([c for c in cfgs if c["model"] == model], key=lambda c: c[axis])
        if not pts:
            continue
        kw = series_kwargs(KEY[model], ls="none")
        ax.plot([c[axis] for c in pts], [c["pressure_l2_mean"] for c in pts], **kw, zorder=3)
        for c in pts:
            ax.plot([c[axis]] * len(c["pressure_l2_seeds"]), c["pressure_l2_seeds"], ls="none", marker="_", color=kw["color"], ms=8, mew=1.1, zorder=4)
        # frontier: best error at or under each budget; label only the lanes that set it
        fx, fy, run, on_front = [], [], float("inf"), []
        for c in pts:
            if c["pressure_l2_mean"] < run:
                on_front.append(c)
            run = min(run, c["pressure_l2_mean"]); fx.append(c[axis]); fy.append(run)
        ax.step(fx, fy, where="post", color=STYLE[KEY[model]]["color"], lw=1.6, alpha=0.55, label="_nolegend_")
        for c in on_front:
            dep = depth_of(c)
            lab = f"{c['width']}x{c['cells'] // 1000}k" + ("" if dep in (8, 12) else f" L{dep}")
            ax.annotate(lab, (c[axis], c["pressure_l2_mean"]), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(6, -10),
                        fontsize=7.5, color=STYLE[KEY[model]]["color"], path_effects=halo())
    d = best.get(("gt_unit", 256, 200000, 12))
    if d:
        ax.plot([d[axis]], [d["pressure_l2_mean"]], marker="o", ms=15, mfc="none", mec=RED, mew=1.4, ls="none", label="GeoTransolver recipe default (256 wide, 200,000 cells)" if ax is axes[0] else "_nolegend_")
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel(xlabel); ax.grid(True, which="both", color=GRID, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
    ticks = [10, 20, 50, 100, 200] if axis == "peak_mem_gb" else [0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0]
    ax.set_xticks(ticks); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{t:g}" for t in ticks]); ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
axes[0].legend(loc="upper right", frameon=False, fontsize=8.2)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-equal-budget
#| output: asis
rows = sorted(cfgs, key=lambda c: (c["model"] != "isla", c["model"], c["params"], c["cells"]))
NAME = {"isla": "ISLA", "gt_unit": "GeoTransolver", "transolver_unit": "Transolver"}
out = "| model | width (parameters) | cells per case | pressure L2, seeds | mean | peak memory [GB] | step p10 / median [s] |\n|---|---|--:|---|--:|--:|---|\n"
for c in rows:
    seeds = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
    lr_s = c["lr"] if "e-" in c["lr"] else c["lr"].replace("e", "e-")  # the ladder keys write 1e-3 as "1e3"
    lr = f", {lr_s}" if c["model"] == "gt_unit" and c["width"] >= 512 else ""
    dep = depth_of(c)
    dep_s = "" if dep in (8, 12) else f", {dep} layers"
    out += (f"| {NAME[c['model']]} | {c['width']} ({c['params'] / 1e6:.1f}M){lr}{dep_s} | {c['cells'] // 1000}k | {seeds} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** | "
            f"{c['peak_mem_gb']:.0f} | {c['step_s_p10']:.2f} / {c['step_s_median']:.2f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Every cost-logged configuration of the cell-count ladder and the width and depth ladders at the default slice count "
      "on the DrivAerML Surface task (435 cars, 500 epochs, two seeds; training cells per case as listed, every row scored in "
      "float32 at 200,000 cells on the 48 validation cars). GeoTransolver is at its better learning rate per configuration. "
      "Costs are per-lane values over the run (memory: peak of the logged per-step values; step: tenth percentile and median) "
      "on one GB300. How to read this: rows differ in width, parameters and cells at once, so a comparison across "
      "architectures must be read at matched memory or matched parameters (@tbl-floor), not down the column. "
      "Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json and results/cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json. {#tbl-equal-budget}")
```

## What compute should buy: cases, parameters, epochs {#sec-compute-allocation}

**On the DrivAerML Surface task, below about 200 training cases every unit
of compute belongs to more cases; past 200 cars the data term of the
fitted law falls below the parameter term and compute goes to width;
epochs buy nothing measurable. On AirfRANS (interior task) the error is a
floorless power law in cases, and cases stay the better purchase across
the range measured.** That is the answer, per dataset, to the question a
language-model practitioner would ask of a surrogate: what is the
compute-optimal mix of training set, model size and training length? The
instrument on DrivAerML is a scaling study: ISLA at three widths and
GeoTransolver at three widths, each trained for 500 epochs at 100,000
cells per case on 27, 54, 109, 218 and 435 cars, two seeds, scored in
float32 (thirty configurations, sixty lanes). @fig-scaling-cases shows
the picture with the fitted law drawn where it is accepted.


```{python}
#| label: tbl-scaling-exponents
#| output: asis
def slope(rows, lo, hi):
    d = {r[0]: r[1] for r in rows}
    return -np.log(d[hi] / d[lo]) / np.log(hi / lo) if lo in d and hi in d else None
out = "| model | width | 27 to 54 cars | 54 to 109 | 109 to 218 | 218 to 435 | parameters, 15x: at 27 / 54 / 109 / 218 / 435 cars |\n|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|\n"
for m, name in (("isla", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver")):
    ws = sorted(pts[m])
    for w in ws:
        rows = pts[m][w]; ss = [slope(rows, a, b) for a, b in ((27, 54), (54, 109), (109, 218), (218, 435))]
        f = lambda s: f"{s:.2f}" if s is not None else "—"
        gains = []
        for n in (27, 54, 109, 218, 435):
            lo = {r[0]: r[1] for r in pts[m][ws[0]]}.get(n); hi = {r[0]: r[1] for r in pts[m][ws[-1]]}.get(n)
            gains.append(f"{100 * (1 - hi / lo):.0f}%" if lo and hi else "—")
        out += f"| {name} | {w} | {' | '.join(f(s) for s in ss)} | {' / '.join(gains) if w == ws[0] else ''} |\n"
out += "\n: Local exponents of the error against training cases on the DrivAerML Surface task (the negative log-log slope between adjacent rungs, at each width) and the gain from a 15x parameter increase (narrowest to widest lane) at each rung. How to read this: a falling local exponent is the signature of an approach to a floor, not of a scale-free law. Data: results/scalelaw_drivaerml_2026-09-22.json. {#tbl-scaling-exponents}\n"
print(out)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scaling-fit
#| output: asis
out = "| model | $\\varepsilon_\\infty$ | $a$ | $\\alpha$ | $b$ | $\\beta$ | RMS residual | accepted (below 3%) | $n^\\ast$ at the recipe width |\n|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|--:|\n"
for m, name in (("isla", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver")):
    F = SLF[f"drivaerml|{m}"]; f = F["fit"]; b = F["bootstrap_p16_p50_p84"]
    rng_ = lambda k: f"{f[k]:.2f} ({b[k][0]:.2f} to {b[k][2]:.2f})"
    floor = f"{f['eps_inf']:.4f} ({b['eps_inf'][0]:.4f} to {b['eps_inf'][2]:.4f})" + (" (on its bound)" if f["eps_inf_on_bound"] else "")
    out += f"| {name} | {floor} | {f['a']:.1f} | {rng_('alpha')} | {f['b']:.0f} | {rng_('beta')} | {100 * f['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}% | {'yes' if F['law_accepted_rms_below_3pct'] else 'no'} | {F['n_star_recipe_width']:.0f} cars |\n"
out += "\n: The fitted law $\\varepsilon = \\varepsilon_\\infty + a\\,n^{-\\alpha} + b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ per architecture on the DrivAerML Surface task (least squares on the relative residual of the seed means; $\\varepsilon_\\infty$ bounded to at most 0.9 times the best measured error; 16th to 84th percentiles of a 400-draw two-seed bootstrap in parentheses). A fit is accepted when its RMS relative residual is below 3%. $n^\\ast$ is the case count at which the data and parameter terms are equal at the recipe width (ISLA 192, GeoTransolver 256). How to read this: GeoTransolver's row is reported but not accepted, so its exponents are indicative and its curve is not drawn in @fig-scaling-cases. Data: results/scalelaw_drivaerml_2026-09-22.json. {#tbl-scaling-fit}\n"
print(out)
```

**Reading the exponents.** The error is not a single power law in the
training-set size: the local exponent falls from about 0.7 to 0.9 between
27 and 54 cars to 0.1 to 0.2 between 218 and 435, for both models
(@tbl-scaling-exponents). That is the signature of an approach to a
floor, and the floor is the one @sec-shared-floor measures directly.
Parameters are cheap by comparison at every rung: a 15x increase buys
each model about a tenth of its error from 54 cars up (@tbl-scaling-exponents),
and the capacity ladders show that a further doubling at 435 cars buys a
few percent before turning over. Epochs are the third axis, and they are
converged (@sec-equal-budget).

**The fitted law.** With five rungs and three widths the Chinchilla form
$\varepsilon = \varepsilon_\infty + a\,n^{-\alpha} + b\,P^{-\beta}$ is
identifiable for ISLA (@tbl-scaling-fit): the floor lands inside its
allowed range, and the fit reproduces the fifteen seed means to
`{python} f"{100 * SLF['drivaerml|isla']['fit']['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}%"`
RMS, under the 3% acceptance bar set in advance. The exponents describe
the *reducible* error above the floor, which is why $\alpha$ is far above
the local slopes of the total error in @tbl-scaling-exponents. For
GeoTransolver the same form misses the bar
(`{python} f"{100 * SLF['drivaerml|gt']['fit']['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}%"`)
and pushes the floor onto its bound, because its 27-car rung is not
monotone in width (the 1,024-wide model is worse than the 512-wide one
there, seeds separated) and an additive law has no term for a wide model
losing to a narrower one at small data; its exponents are nonetheless
within the bootstrap spread of ISLA's
(`{python} "same" if SLD['bars']['drivaerml']['exponents_same']['alpha']['same'] and SLD['bars']['drivaerml']['exponents_same']['beta']['same'] else "different"`
within the bootstrap on both). **The two architectures convert cases and
parameters into accuracy at the same rates on this task**;
GeoTransolver's small-data lead (@sec-data-efficiency) is an offset in
the coefficients, not a slope. ISLA shows the same non-monotonicity in
milder form at 27 cars, so the effect is not one architecture's.

**The compute-optimal rule this implies.** Training compute in this
recipe is proportional to parameters times tokens seen, $C \propto P
\cdot n \cdot c \cdot E$ with $n$ cases, $c$ cells per case and $E$
epochs; cells are flat above 100,000 and epochs are converged
(@sec-equal-budget), so the question reduces to $P$ against $n$ at fixed
$P \cdot n$. In the Chinchilla form the optimum grows the axis with the
*smaller* exponent once the other's term is driven down, $P^\ast \propto
C^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}$ and $n^\ast \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)}$;
with ISLA's $\alpha \approx 1.3$ and $\beta \approx 0.5$ this puts about
70% of each compute increment into parameters *once the data term is the
smaller one*, and the crossover is where the two fitted terms are equal
at the recipe width:
`{python} f"{SLF['drivaerml|isla']['n_star_recipe_width']:.0f}"` cars
for ISLA (@tbl-scaling-fit). Below that count the data term dominates and
every unit of compute belongs to cases; above it the residual data term
is a few thousandths and compute goes to width or depth until the floor.
The rule in one line: *collect cases until about 200, then widen.* Two
practical consequences: on a dataset of a few hundred cases the recipe's
width is the right place to spend, and a claim that one architecture
"scales better" needs the exponents, not a single-width ladder.

**The same axis on a second dataset and task.** On AirfRANS
(two-dimensional incompressible airfoil flow, the interior task of
@sec-interior-airfrans) the training-case axis runs over nested subsets
of 50, 100, 200, 400 and 800 airfoils for ISLA at 192 wide and
GeoTransolver-volume, two seeds each, 500 epochs at 100,000 interior
queries (@fig-scaling-airfrans). The curve has a different shape there:
no floor within reach at 800 airfoils, and ISLA's error falls as a clean
power law $n^{-\alpha}$ on pressure and velocity ($\alpha$ =
`{python} f"{J('airfrans_scale_2026-09-22.json')['fits']['isla|pressure_l2']['fit']['alpha']:.2f}"`
on pressure,
`{python} f"{J('airfrans_scale_2026-09-22.json')['fits']['isla|velocity_l2']['fit']['alpha']:.2f}"`
on velocity, both fits accepted). GeoTransolver-volume's local exponent
on pressure is about 0.5 from 100 airfoils up (its 50-airfoil error sits
above its own trend, so no fit is accepted for it), so **on the one task
where the two architectures' exponents differ, ISLA has the larger one**:
GeoTransolver-volume's pressure lead is
`{python} f"{100 * (1 - J('airfrans_scale_2026-09-22.json')['bars']['ordering']['pressure_l2']['per_rung']['100']['gt_over_isla']):.0f}%"`
at 100 airfoils and
`{python} f"{100 * (1 - J('airfrans_scale_2026-09-22.json')['bars']['ordering']['pressure_l2']['per_rung']['800']['gt_over_isla']):.0f}%"`
at 800, while ISLA's velocity lead holds near 2x from 200 airfoils up. Two
consequences for the rule above. The exponents are properties of a
dataset and a task, not of an architecture, and do not transfer (1.28 for
the reducible error on the cars, 0.67 for the total error on the
airfoils); a compute-allocation rule has to be measured where it will be
used. And the compute-optimal crossover moves with the exponent: with no
floor and $\alpha \approx 0.67$ the data term never becomes small, and
cases stay the better purchase across the whole AirfRANS range measured.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scaling-airfrans
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Interior error against training airfoils on AirfRANS (interior task)
#|   for ISLA (192 wide, 1e-3) and GeoTransolver-volume (1e-3), 500 epochs
#|   at 100,000 interior queries, two-seed means with the seeds as short
#|   bars, float32 on the 200 test airfoils; left, pressure; middle,
#|   velocity; right, eddy viscosity (a standardized field, so its ratios
#|   are orderings under that centering, not physical percentages). Dotted
#|   curves are the fitted $\varepsilon = \varepsilon_\infty + a
#|   n^{-\alpha}$, drawn only where the fit's RMS relative residual is
#|   below 3% (ISLA on pressure and velocity); every other series is
#|   points only, with its local exponents from 100 airfoils up written
#|   beside it. How to read this: parallel point runs mean the same
#|   exponent (velocity); converging runs mean ISLA converts cases faster
#|   (pressure). It does not show a parameter axis (one width per
#|   architecture). Both axes are logarithmic and span the measured range.
#|   Data: results/airfrans_scale_2026-09-22.json.
#| fig-alt: "Three log-log panels of interior error against training airfoils from 50 to 800: ISLA in blue squares with dotted fitted lines on pressure and velocity, GeoTransolver-volume in red circles as points only."
#| code-fold: true
AFS = J("airfrans_scale_2026-09-22.json"); AC = AFS["configurations"]; AFF = AFS["fits"]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(11.0, 3.9), sharex=True)
nn = np.geomspace(45, 900, 100)
for ax, (f, lab) in zip(axes, (("pressure_l2", "interior pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "interior velocity"), ("nut_l2", "interior eddy viscosity"))):
    for m, key in (("isla", "isla_ref"), ("gt", "gt")):
        kw = series_kwargs(key)
        rows = sorted([(c["n"], c[f]["mean"], c[f]["seeds"]) for c in AC.values() if c["arm"] == m and c["status"] == "complete" and f in c])
        ax.plot([r[0] for r in rows], [r[1] for r in rows], marker=kw["marker"], color=kw["color"], ls="none", ms=6, label=STYLE[key]["label"] + ("-volume" if m == "gt" else ""))
        for r in rows:
            ax.plot([r[0]] * len(r[2]), r[2], ls="none", marker="_", color=kw["color"], ms=7, mew=1.1)
        F = AFF[f"{m}|{f}"]["fit"]; accepted = F["rms_rel_residual"] < 0.03
        loc = AFF[f"{m}|{f}"]["local_alpha"]; tail = [v for k, v in loc.items() if int(k.split("-")[0]) >= 100]
        if accepted:
            ax.plot(nn, F["eps_inf"] + F["a"] * nn ** (-F["alpha"]), color=kw["color"], ls=":", lw=1.1, zorder=0)
            lab_a = f"α = {F['alpha']:.2f} (fit)"
        else:
            lab_a = f"local α {min(tail):.2f} to {max(tail):.2f}"
        ax.text(rows[-1][0] * 1.08, rows[-1][1], lab_a, fontsize=8, color=kw["color"], va="bottom" if m == "isla" else "top")
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xticks([50, 100, 200, 400, 800]); ax.set_xticklabels(["50", "100", "200", "400", "800"])
    ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
    ax.set_yticks([0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2]); ax.set_yticklabels(["0.02", "0.03", "0.05", "0.10", "0.20"]); ax.set_xlim(42, 1500)
    ax.set_xlabel("training airfoils [count]"); ax.set_ylabel(f"{lab} relative L2 error [–]")
axes[1].plot([], [], color=INK2, ls=":", lw=1.1, label="dotted: fitted law (accepted fits only)")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Cost {#sec-cost-sweep}


**At the recipe widths the three architectures are parameter-matched
(ISLA `{python} f"{ISO['isla|w192|c200k|lr1e-3|ep500']['params'] / 1e6:.1f}M"`,
GeoTransolver `{python} f"{ISO['gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500']['params'] / 1e6:.1f}M"`,
Transolver `{python} f"{ISO['transolver_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500']['params'] / 1e6:.1f}M"`),
and with the fused geometry kernel, the default on CUDA, ISLA's training
step tracks GeoTransolver's at every token count in about half its
memory.** The token budget decides the cost comparison more than the
architecture does. @fig-cost-sweep sweeps the training step from 2,500 to
200,000 tokens per case on the compiled path every model trains on, and
extends the memory axis to 600,000 cells with the training logs of the
cell-count ladder. GeoTransolver's step is nearly flat below 40,000
tokens, where the GPU is not saturated, and grows to about twice its
10,000-token value at the recipe's default of 200,000. ISLA with the
fused geometry kernel (`geo_kernel=None` resolves to it on CUDA,
@sec-using-cost) tracks GeoTransolver's step at every count; on the
fallback path, the eager geometry region with its per-slice invariants
recomputed in the backward pass, the step grows linearly from 20,000
tokens on and is about five times GeoTransolver's at 200,000. At the
recipe default of 200,000 cells every model fits one GB300; at 400,000
cells GeoTransolver-256's training-log peak is
`{python} f"{ISO['gt_unit|w256|c400k|lr3e-3|ep500']['peak_mem_gb']:.0f}"` GB
against ISLA-192's
`{python} f"{ISO['isla|w192|c400k|lr1e-3|ep500']['peak_mem_gb']:.0f}"` GB,
and ISLA at 600,000 cells trains in
`{python} f"{ISO['isla|w192|c600k|lr1e-3|ep500']['peak_mem_gb']:.0f}"` GB,
about what GeoTransolver-256 needs at 200,000. The per-configuration
footprint table of the shipped configurations is @sec-using-cost.

```{python}
#| label: fig-cost-sweep
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Training-step time (top) and peak memory (bottom) against the number
#|   of tokens per case, 2,500 to 600,000, for the two ISLA reference
#|   candidates (384 wide with 12 layers, solid blue; with 24 layers,
#|   dash-dot blue), ISLA at 192 wide (pale blue), GeoTransolver at 256
#|   (red) and 512 wide (light red) and Transolver at 256 wide (amber).
#|   Lines: one GB300, bf16 autocast, batch of one case, AdamW step
#|   included, every model compiled, ISLA with the fused geometry kernel,
#|   median of ten measured steps after warm-up on random inputs; memory is
#|   the allocator's peak during the step. Crosses (bottom): the peak memory
#|   logged over a full 500-epoch training run of the cell-count ladder
#|   (@tbl-cells-ladder), a different instrument that includes the
#|   allocator's reserve and the data pipeline. How to read this: all axes
#|   are logarithmic and the lines are joined measurements, not fits; below
#|   about 40,000 tokens every model is launch-bound and the lines are flat;
#|   the 200,000-token column is the reporting protocol and its numbers are
#|   in @tbl-cost-200k; the training lanes of this book are dominated by
#|   data loading, so the top panel ranks the models' step cost, not their
#|   wall-clock. Data: results/cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json;
#|   results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json.
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked log-log panels against tokens per case from 2,500 to 600,000: step time and peak memory, six lines each, plus crosses from training logs on the memory panel."
#| code-fold: true
import statistics as st
CSR = J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")
CS = CSR["runs"]
GIB_TO_GB = 1024 ** 3 / 1e9
COST_ARMS = [("isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref", "ISLA 384 x 12 (reference candidate R1)", dict(color=BLUE, ls="-")),
             ("isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused", "isla_ref", "ISLA 384 x 24 (reference candidate R2)", dict(color=BLUE, ls="-.")),
             ("isla_192x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref", "ISLA 192 x 12", dict(color=BLUE_PALE, ls="-")),
             ("geotransolver_256", "gt", "GeoTransolver 256 (recipe default)", dict(color=RED, ls="-")),
             ("geotransolver_512", "gt", "GeoTransolver 512", dict(color=RED_LIGHT, ls="-")),
             ("transolver_256", "t", "Transolver 256", {})]
fig, (ax0, ax1) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 7.0), sharex=True, gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.08))
for arm, key, lab, ov in COST_ARMS:
    rows = sorted([r for r in CS if r["arm"] == arm and r["status"] == "ok"], key=lambda r: r["tokens"])
    xs = [r["tokens"] for r in rows]
    ax0.plot(xs, [st.median(r["step_ms"]) for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, **ov))
    ax1.plot(xs, [r["peak_allocated_gib"] * GIB_TO_GB for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, **ov))
# training-log peaks of the cell-count ladder (per-lane peak over the run), marked as a distinct instrument
for model, key, width, lr in (("isla", "isla_ref", 192, "1e-3"), ("gt_unit", "gt", 256, "3e-3"), ("transolver_unit", "t", 256, "3e-3")):
    rows = sorted([c for c in ISO.values() if c["model"] == model and c["width"] == width and c["epochs"] == 500 and c["lr"] == lr and c.get("peak_mem_gb")], key=lambda c: c["cells"])
    ax1.plot([c["cells"] for c in rows], [c["peak_mem_gb"] for c in rows], ls="none", marker="x", ms=9, mew=2.0, color=STYLE[key]["color"], zorder=4)
ax1.plot([], [], ls="none", marker="x", ms=9, mew=2.0, color=INK2, label="training-log peak, 500-epoch run (192 / 256 wide)")
for ax in (ax0, ax1):
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.grid(True, which="major", color=GRID); ax.grid(False, which="minor")
    ax.axvline(200000, color=BASELINE, lw=1.0, zorder=0)
ax0.set_yscale("log"); ax1.set_yscale("log")
ax0.set_ylabel("training step [ms]"); ax1.set_ylabel("peak GPU memory [GB]")
ax0.set_yticks([20, 50, 100, 200, 500]); ax0.set_yticklabels(["20", "50", "100", "200", "500"])
ax1.set_yticks([0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200]); ax1.set_yticklabels(["0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "20", "50", "100", "200"])
ax1.set_xlim(2000, 800000)
ax1.set_xticks([2500, 10000, 40000, 100000, 200000, 400000, 600000]); ax1.set_xticklabels(["2,500", "10,000", "40,000", "100,000", "200,000", "400,000", "\n600,000"])
ax1.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax0.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax1.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax1.set_xlabel("tokens per case [count]")
ax0.text(200000, ax0.get_ylim()[0], " reporting protocol", fontsize=8, color=INK2, va="bottom")
ax0.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8.2); ax1.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8.0)
plt.show()
```
